html:
The Apalachee were a farming people of the Florida Panhandle, between the Aucilla and Ochlockonee rivers around present Tallahassee. They grew maize in large fields and lived in chiefdoms of the Mississippian kind, related to the Mississippian towns to the north, with platform mounds at their centres.

Hernando de Soto and his army spent the winter of 1539 to 1540 in their main town, Anhaica. From 1633 Franciscan missions spread among them, and Apalachee maize fed Spanish St. Augustine in Florida.

In 1704 raiders from English Carolina under James Moore, with Creek allies, destroyed the missions. Many Apalachee were killed or enslaved; others fled to Pensacola and Mobile and later to Louisiana, where a small community remains. Earlier maps show them as Apalachee; their neighbours to the east were the Timucua.
